name: Brazil
genZNote: Brazil is so big it borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador — and it's the only major nation on the continent where Portuguese, not Spanish, is spoken, a direct legacy of a 1494 treaty that split the 'New World' between two European kingdoms.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: The largest country in South America by both area and population, home to the majority of the Amazon Rainforest, the world's largest tropical rainforest.
Borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador, with an extensive Atlantic coastline.
Home to the Amazon River, the world's largest river by discharge volume, and vast biodiversity across multiple distinct ecosystems (Amazon, Cerrado savanna, Pantanal wetlands).

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Portuguese is the official language, making Brazil the only major Portuguese-speaking nation in the Americas, a legacy of the 1494 Treaty of Tordesillas dividing colonial claims.
A highly multicultural society shaped by Indigenous, Portuguese colonial, African (via the historic slave trade), and later European and Asian immigrant influences.
World-renowned for Carnival celebrations, samba music, and football, which holds a central place in national identity and global sporting success.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal presidential republic composed of 26 states and a Federal District, with a President serving as both head of state and government.
Gained independence from Portugal in 1822, and transitioned from monarchy to republic in 1889 and later from military rule (1964-1985) to full democracy.
Brasília, a purpose-built modernist capital city inaugurated in 1960, was designed to encourage development of the country's interior.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A significant hub for tropical disease research and biodiversity science, given the scale and ecological importance of the Amazon.
Home to Embraer, one of the world's largest aircraft manufacturers, reflecting a strong aerospace engineering sector.
Advanced agricultural science (Embrapa) transformed vast tropical savanna (Cerrado) into some of the world's most productive farmland, a globally studied agricultural technology success.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A founding BRICS member (alongside Brazil, Russia, India, China, and now expanded membership) and G20 member, representing Latin America's largest economy and voice on the global stage.
Plays a central role in Amazon rainforest conservation diplomacy, given its stewardship of the majority of this globally critical carbon sink.
A leading voice in Latin American regional organisations including Mercosur and a vocal advocate for UN Security Council reform.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Brazil are both founding BRICS members and share a 'Strategic Partnership', collaborating closely on pharmaceuticals, agriculture, biofuels, and defence.
Brazil is a major global producer of generic pharmaceuticals and biofuels (ethanol), areas of significant cooperation potential with India.
Both countries are part of the IBSA Dialogue Forum (India-Brazil-South Africa), advocating jointly for reform of global governance institutions like the UN Security Council.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: Latin America's largest economy, a major global exporter of soybeans, beef, coffee, iron ore, and sugar/ethanol.
Home to Embraer (aircraft manufacturing) and a globally significant agribusiness sector built on Cerrado savanna agricultural technology.
A member of BRICS and Mercosur, playing a central role in South American regional economic integration.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Hosting the majority of the Amazon Rainforest, a globally critical ecosystem and carbon sink.
Carnival, samba, and being a football (soccer) powerhouse with the most FIFA World Cup titles.
Being Latin America's largest economy and a founding BRICS member.
Purpose-built modernist capital city, Brasília.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Brazilian Real (BRL).
Largest economy in South America, led by agribusiness (soybeans, coffee, beef, sugarcane), mining (iron ore), and manufacturing.
Among the world's top producers and exporters of coffee, soybeans, and orange juice.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Holds the majority of the Amazon Rainforest, the world's largest tropical rainforest and a critical global carbon sink.
The Pantanal is the world's largest tropical wetland, hosting exceptional wildlife biodiversity.
Faces significant deforestation pressure alongside major conservation and reforestation initiatives.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Colonized by Portugal from 1500; became the seat of the Portuguese Empire in 1808 when the royal court relocated there.
Declared independence in 1822, initially as the Empire of Brazil under a monarchy.
Became a republic in 1889; a military dictatorship ruled from 1964 to 1985 before a return to democracy.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1988 Constitution, known as the 'Citizen Constitution', was adopted after the end of military rule, establishing a federal presidential republic.
Brasília, a purpose-built planned capital, replaced Rio de Janeiro as the capital in 1960.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (INPE) leads space research; the Alcântara Launch Center is used for satellite launches.
Embrapa (Brazilian Agricultural Research Corporation) is a global leader in tropical agriculture research.
A pioneer in biofuel technology, producing ethanol from sugarcane at large scale.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Football is a defining national passion — a record five-time FIFA World Cup champion, home to Pelé.
Carnival and samba are globally recognised cultural exports centred on Rio de Janeiro.
Hosted the 2014 FIFA World Cup and the 2016 Summer Olympics.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding UN member; part of BRICS, the G20, and Mercosur.
A vocal advocate for reform and a permanent seat on the UN Security Council.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Brazil is South America's largest country, a federal presidential republic and founding BRICS member, home to most of the Amazon Rainforest and the only Portuguese-speaking nation in the Americas.
keyFacts: Federal presidential republic; 26 states plus a Federal District.
Home to the majority of the Amazon Rainforest and Amazon River.
Founding BRICS member; Latin America's largest economy.
commonConfusion: Brazil's official language is Portuguese, not Spanish — a direct legacy of the 1494 Treaty of Tordesillas dividing South America between Portugal and Spain.

highYieldFacts: Brazil: federal presidential republic; capital Brasília; only major Portuguese-speaking nation in the Americas.
Hosts the majority of the Amazon Rainforest; founding BRICS member; Latin America's largest economy.
India-Brazil: BRICS and IBSA partners; cooperate on pharmaceuticals, biofuels, agriculture, and UNSC reform advocacy.
commonTraps: Assuming Brazil speaks Spanish like most of Latin America — it speaks Portuguese.
Confusing Brazil's capital (Brasília) with its most famous cities (Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo).
mustRemember: Brazil: Portuguese-speaking, Amazon steward, founding BRICS/IBSA member, top agri-exporter, key India strategic partner.
